title: Microbes, not plants, first filled Earth’s air with oxygen
body: For roughly the first half of Earth’s history the air held almost no free oxygen. Photosynthetic microbes, above all cyanobacteria, released oxygen as a waste product, and beginning about 2.4 billion years ago it started to build up in the atmosphere and shallow seas, a shift called the Great Oxidation Event. The new gas was probably toxic to many existing microbes, but it eventually made oxygen-breathing life like ours possible.

slides.question: How long ago did oxygen start to build up in Earth’s atmosphere?
slides.explanation: About 2.4 billion years ago, in the Great Oxidation Event. For roughly the first half of Earth’s history, the air held almost no free oxygen.

slides.heading: Earth’s history, in billions of years ago
slides.note: The Great Oxidation Event began when Earth was roughly half its present age

slides.clue: The photosynthetic microbes that first filled Earth’s air with oxygen
slides.detail: From the Greek kyanos, ‘blue’: they are also called blue-green algae, though they are bacteria, not algae.
